title: Friday: Jumu'ah
hook: Once a week, the whole community prays together. Here's what happens, so you can walk in ready.

screens.text: Friday is the Muslim week's big day. At midday the masjid fills up for **Jumu'ah**, the Friday prayer. It's the best place to feel part of the community, and today you'll know exactly what to expect.

**Jumu'ah takes the place of Dhuhr on Fridays.** The Qur'an says: when the call to Friday prayer is made, hurry to remember Allah and set your business aside [Q 62:9]. Once it's over, go back to your day [Q 62:10].
bubbles: The whole thing usually takes 30–45 minutes. {{masjid.name}}'s time: **{{masjid.jumuah_time}}**.

screens.title: Two rak'ahs behind the imam
screens.intro: After the sermon, line up and follow the imam, just as on Day 7.

moves.text: Line up in the row. In your heart, intend to pray Jumu'ah behind the imam.
After the imam says *Allahu akbar*, say it too.
Stand silently and listen while he recites aloud.
Bow just after he bows, and rise when he rises.
Prostrate just after him, twice, as in every rak'ah. Then the second rak'ah, the same way.
After the second rak'ah, sit and say what you know, as you do at the end of every prayer.
When he ends with the salam, say it after him, to the right…
…and to the left. That's Jumu'ah: no Dhuhr today.

screens.done_text: Two rak'ahs together, and you're done.

screens.text: **What else you'll see.** Many people pray a few extra rak'ahs on their own, before and after. That's optional for you for now (Day 57). Afterwards, stay a few minutes and say salam: this is where you meet people.

aiContext:
**Lesson facts**
- Hurry to Friday prayer when it's called, leaving trade; after it, return to work [Q 62:9–10].
- Jumu'ah is obligatory on adult, sane, resident men without an excuse; women, travelers and the sick are exempt, and if they attend it counts; it replaces Dhuhr [IslamQA 2905; IslamWeb 82835; First Instructions on Worship]. Whoever misses it prays Dhuhr.
- Structure: adhan, two sermons with a brief sitting between, iqamah, two rak'ahs led aloud [First Instructions on Worship].
- Bathing for Jumu'ah [Bukhari 877]; silence during the khutbah [Bukhari 934].
- Hanafi: Jumu'ah is held in a town or city with conditions; sunnah prayers before (4) and after (4, and in some views 2 more) are sunnah mu'akkadah. Don't teach these now.
- US: employees may request religious accommodation for Friday prayer (Day 24) [Welcome to Islam D5].

**Likely questions**
- *"I'm a guy and work Fridays."* Jumu'ah is required for him; look for a nearby masjid or a workplace Jumu'ah, ask for a long lunch and make up the time (Day 24). If truly impossible, escalate; meanwhile he prays Dhuhr.
- *"Arabic sermon?"* Listen; meaning isn't required for the prayer to count; many masjids give an English summary.
- *"Arrived during the sermon?"* Sit quietly and listen; in the Hanafi school, don't start a prayer once the imam has begun the sermon.
- *"Arrived after the prayer started?"* Join; ask how to complete (Day 22).
- *"What to wear?"* Clean, modest, your nicest clothes; nothing special required.
- *Teen at school:* boys past puberty are obliged; route school conflicts to the mentor.

**Escalate:** a man whose job makes Jumu'ah impossible every week; a student whose school won't release him.

**Don't:** tell a woman she must attend; tell a man he can skip it for convenience; give legal advice on accommodation.
madhabNote: All four schools agree Jumu'ah is required of resident adult men and replaces Dhuhr. They differ on details: how many people are needed for it to be held (Hanafi: at least three plus the imam; Maliki: twelve; Shafi'i and Hanbali: forty), and whether it may be held outside a town. Basmala: Hanafis and Hanbalis say it quietly before al-Fatiha and don't count it as one of its verses; Shafi'is count it as the first verse and say it aloud in the audible prayers; Malikis don't say it in obligatory prayers.
